name: Jackson, Mississippi, 30 June 2014 (evening balloon)
line: Very unstable summer air (CAPE about 3300 J/kg) with almost no wind aloft (3 m/s of shear over 6 km): storms rise, rain and collapse.
note: The balloon launched at 0000 UTC on 1 July (7 pm local time on 30 June). Picked by a stated rule (July, unstable, less than 8 m/s of shear) from Gulf Coast evening balloons. The storm is started by a gentle push of rising air, as CM1's updraft nudging does. In a 1 km run the storm rises, rains and collapses within about 35 minutes (measured). This day's sounding in an idealized storm, not a reconstruction of that day's storms. The area is not made smaller than 120 km, because CM1's parcel grid covers 120 km; the fit makes the grid coarser or the storm shorter instead.

90 minutes: storms in calm air live and die within an hour
a restart point every 30 minutes, which divides the 90 minutes
netCDF, which ncview, xarray and most tools read (CM1's file asks for GrADS)

the sounding is the file input_sounding beside this namelist

follow air parcels, so Results can show air rising into the storm
CM1's own parcel grid: 60 x 60 across, every 2 km, and 10 levels, every 1 km
CM1's updraft nudging starts the storm: a gentle push of rising air for its first 20 minutes (Naylor and Gilmore 2012), with CM1's own strength, size and timing
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)

gm1_settings_why: The push of rising air that starts the storm is centred 4.5 km west and 2.1 km north of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the nudging's centre in its code (xc_wnudge, yc_wnudge), not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.
